newsitem.title: CUBA: Cuban officers pledge loyalty to revolution.
newsitem.headline: Cuban officers pledge loyalty to revolution.

text.p: President Fidel Castro has received a pledge of loyalty signed by a quarter of a million active and reserve officers of Cuba's armed forces, State Security and police, Juventud Rebelde reported on Sunday.
It said the pledge of "patriotic and revolutionary loyalty" was presented to Castro in a ceremony at Revolution Square on Saturday.

The pledge, in the form of a written declaration, angrily rejected a U.S policy paper issued by the Clinton administration in January calling on Castro's government to resign to open the way toward a multi-party government and capitalist economy.

"They propose that we give our country to the empire and the counterrevolutionary and annexationist mafia of Miami so that they can tear it to shreds", the declaration stated. In Cuban government jargon, the word "empire" refers to the United States.

The declaration went on: "...we cannot permit orders being being given to our nation as if it were a colonial appendage of the United States and we will not now accept or ever accept orders from Washington or anyone else".

The pledge referred to the fear expressed in writing by Jose Marti before his death in 1895 that the United States sought to exercise its hegemony over Cuba. Jose Marti, known as "the Apostle of Cuban Independence" organised the final phase of the islands long war against Spanish colonialism and was killed in battle in May, 1895.

The officers' declaration is the latest salvo of a campaign within Cuba to condemn the Helms-Burton bill which was signed into law by President Clinton in March 1996. The law overtly calls for the overthrow of Cuba's revolutionary government and applies legal sanctions against foreign enterprises and governments who do not adhere to the thirty-five year old U.S embargo on trade and financial relations with the Caribbean island.
Open opposition to the Helm-Burton law has been expressed by dozens of nations including members of the European Community, Canada, Russia and Mexico.
